title: What signs show that a company has outgrown manual WhatsApp and needs native automation?
summary: See which signs show that a company has outgrown manual WhatsApp and needs native automation.
body_text: Companies still running things through a personal WhatsApp number or loose group chats eventually notice that the volume of conversations has outgrown their manual control — and that's the point where WhatsApp automation with AI agents in Jestor starts making a real difference in the operation. The symptoms of a WhatsApp gone out of control Excessive manual work on WhatsApp is one of the most common pain points cited by operations leaders: conversations get lost, no one knows who already answered what, and support depends on a single person with access to the number. With no system behind it, every new client or process that goes through WhatsApp becomes one more variable out of control, with no centralized history and no response-time tracking. What native automation solves in this scenario Every new incoming message automatically creates a card in the linked process. Visual indicators show who last responded, team or customer. Time spent in each phase of the conversation gets tracked, like an SLA. AI agents can respond automatically, with a human stepping in when needed. Setup takes less than five minutes, via the official Meta API. Jestor connects WhatsApp Business natively via the official Meta API, turning every conversation into a manageable card, like a CRM or a support hub — WhatsApp stops being a blind spot in the operation and becomes just another structured channel within the system. Frequently Asked Questions How long does it take to set up the WhatsApp integration? Setup takes less than five minutes, requiring a Jestor account, a WhatsApp number, and a Facebook Business account. Can the AI agent respond on WhatsApp with no human oversight? Yes, but Jestor also supports human-in-the-loop, letting a human join the conversation when needed. Can each department have its own WhatsApp number? Yes, Jestor supports multiple numbers, each linked to a specific table or process. title: Collaboration with Stanford GMP Facility
body_text: We're excited to share that we are establishing a collaboration with Stanford GMP Facility: Laboratory for Cell and Gene Medicine (LCGM) to deploy our robotic systems for cell therapy manufacturing. Combining LCGM's unmatched process development expertise with our robotic technology enables cell therapy organizations to run side-by-side comparisons of their current manual processes with the corresponding automated processes. We can't wait for cell therapy leaders to see what's possible with automation as we take another step forward to reducing barriers to patient access to cell therapies.

title: Pyka and Foundation for California Community Colleges Awarded CARB and CEC Grant for Commercial-Scale Zero-Emission Autonomous Aviation Demonstration in California Agriculture
summary: Pyka and Foundation for California Community Colleges Awarded CARB and CEC Grant for Commercial-Scale Zero-Emission Autonomous Aviation Demonstration in California Agriculture
body_text: Pyka and Foundation for California Community Colleges Awarded CARB and CEC Grant for Commercial-Scale Zero-Emission Autonomous Aviation Demonstration in California Agriculture ‍ ALAMEDA, Calif., April, 15, 2026 — Pyka, a California-based leader in autonomous electric aviation, today announced it will serve as the lead technology partner on the California Zero-Emission Aviation Demonstration Project. The project is funded by California Climate Investments through the California Air Resources Board’s Sustainable Heavy-Duty Initiatives for Future Technology (SHIFT) program and supported by the California Energy Commission (CEC). Administered by the Foundation for California Community Colleges (FoundationCCC), the project will deploy one of the first large-scale commercial demonstrations of all-electric, autonomous aircraft in California agriculture. The multi-year project will demonstrate the real-world viability of zero-emission aviation by deploying Pyka’s all-electric autonomous Pelican 2 aircraft. The aircraft will operate under Federal Aviation Administration approvals for agricultural operations at Victoria Island Farms in California’s Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta. Power will come primarily from off-grid solar charging systems, with additional support from project-funded zero-emission ground-support vehicles. Together, these systems will significantly reduce fossil fuel use associated with both flight operations and on-site agricultural support. The project brings together partners from industry, agriculture, and workforce development, including Pyka, Victoria Island Farms, Ogive Technology, Inc., NPower California, and the Bay Area Community College Consortium (BACCC). “This project will demonstrate the scalability of zero-emission autonomous aircraft,” said Chuma Ogunwole, Chief Operating Officer of Pyka. “By operating autonomous electric aircraft at commercial scale in a real agricultural environment, we’re proving that aviation can reduce emissions today — not decades from now — while improving safety, efficiency, and community outcomes.” ‍ Advancing CARB’s Climate, Equity, and Technology Goals The California Zero-Emission Aviation Demonstration Project is part of California Climate Investments, a statewide initiative that uses Cap-and-Invest funds to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, strengthen the economy and improve public health and the environment, particularly in disadvantaged communities. Over the course of the project, operations with Pyka’s aircraft are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by more than 1,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide. The project is also expected to reduce nitrogen oxides (NOx), particulate matter and other criteria pollutants by displacing conventional fossil-fuel-powered crop dusters and diesel agricultural equipment. Additional benefits may include reduced noise pollution, improved application precision that can lower overall chemical use, and reduced spray drift in nearby communities. “California’s responsibility to protect its citizens from harmful air pollution and the effects of climate change extends beyond cars and trucks,” said CARB Deputy Executive Officer of Mobile Sources & Incentives Christopher Grundler. “CARB investments in SHIFT projects like this one are taking zero-emissions technology to new heights and demonstrating that clean aviation is not only feasible, but already capable of doing many jobs better and cheaper than polluting alternatives.” “The CEC is proud to fund the deployment of zero-emission aviation infrastructure for this pilot project,” said Melanie Vail, Deputy Director of the CEC Fuels and Transportation Division. “Zero-emission aviation is California’s next frontier, and this off-grid solar charging system could become an industry blueprint.” The project also includes an equity-centered workforce development and training program, led by FoundationCCC in partnership with NPower California and BACCC. Through paid work experience, professional training pathways, and community college engagement, the program aims to prepare California residents for skilled, living-wage jobs in zero-emission aviation manufacturing and operations. “This project reflects the kind of collaboration California needs to advance innovative technologies alongside workforce and economic development,” said Dr. Jeffrey Clary, Senior Director of Climate Strategies at the Foundation for California Community Colleges. “By combining zero-emission aviation with workforce initiatives, we’re working to deliver air quality benefits while building pathways into high-quality clean jobs in agriculture and aviation. FoundationCCC is proud to partner with Pyka and the project team on this first-of-its-kind demonstration.” ‍ Building a Scalable Model for Zero-Emission Aviation Pyka will manufacture and operate the aircraft from its Bay Area facility in Alameda, California, collecting detailed operational data throughout the demonstration. The data will support reporting to CARB and the CEC and help inform future policy development, regulatory pathways, and industry adoption. The project is designed as a replicable model that can be scaled across California’s agricultural sector and adapted to additional aviation uses, including cargo logistics and other critical services. Broader deployment could amplify long-term emissions reductions statewide and beyond. “This investment demonstrates California’s leadership in tackling some of the most challenging decarbonization challenges,” Ogunwole added. “Aviation has long been one of the most difficult sectors to electrify. This project shows that with the right partners and technology, zero-emission flight is no longer a distant goal – it’s taking shape today.” ‍ About Pyka: Pyka is a robotics company on a mission to build the most useful autonomous aircraft on Earth. At the core of every Pyka aircraft is a vertically integrated aircraft-first robotics stack: proprietary flight control software, avionics, high-power density electric motors, motor controllers, batteries, and carbon fiber composite airframes, developed entirely in-house and manufactured in the United States of America. Learn more at www.flypyka.com . ‍ ‍ ‍ About the Foundation for California Community Colleges (FoundationCCC): The Foundation for California Community Colleges works to benefit students, colleges, and communities by accelerating paths to economic and social mobility, strengthening communities, and reducing barriers to opportunities for all Californians. FoundationCCC is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt non-profit organization founded in 1998. It serves as the official statewide nonprofit organization supporting the California Community Colleges, the largest system of higher education in the nation. For more information, visit www.foundationccc.org . ‍ About the California Air Resources Board (CARB) and Sustainable Heavy-Duty Initiatives for Future Technology (SHIFT) : This project is part of SHIFT, a program administered by the California Air Resources Board and funded through California Climate Investments. CARB's mission is to promote and protect public health, welfare, and ecological resources through effective reduction of air pollutants while recognizing and considering effects on the economy. CARB is the lead agency for climate change programs and oversees all air pollution control efforts in California to attain and maintain health-based air quality standards. SHIFT is an incentive program administered by the California Air Resources Board (CARB) supporting the development and demonstration of advanced, low- and zero-emission technologies for heavy-duty vehicles, off-road equipment, and goods movement. Formerly known as Advanced Technology Demonstration and Pilot Projects, SHIFT investments help accelerate the transition of emerging technologies from pre-commercial demonstration to commercially available options by supporting early deployments and at-scale testing in real-world use. As a part of CARB’s Clean Transportation Incentives, SHIFT projects advance innovative on- and off-road solutions that reduce air pollution, improve public health and support California’s climate and air quality goals. ‍ ‍ ‍ About California Climate Investments: California Climate Investments uses billions of Cap-and-Invest dollars to fund projects that reduce harmful emissions, protect public health, strengthen local economies, and support natural environments. With a strong focus on communities most impacted by pollution and limited access to resources, California Climate Investments helps build a more equitable and sustainable future. ‍ ‍ About the California Energy Commission (CEC): The California Energy Commission supports the implementation of the SHIFT projects by contributing from its Emerging Opportunities fund for the purchase and installation of supporting infrastructure and workforce development investments. The California Energy Commission is the state's primary energy policy and planning agency. It has seven core responsibilities: advancing state energy policy, encouraging energy efficiency, certifying power plants, investing in energy innovation, developing renewable energy, transforming transportation, and preparing for energy emergencies. ‍

title: Spatial Audio vs Dolby Atmos: Which Is Better for Headphones?
summary: Spatial audio vs Dolby Atmos compared for headphones and gaming. What each does, how they differ, and which one delivers better positional audio in 2026.
body_text: Spatial audio and Dolby Atmos are often thrown around as if they mean the same thing, but they do not. One is a broad category of technology, the other is a specific product inside that category. The two are not competing technologies. Dolby Atmos is a specific format within the broader spatial audio category, and confusing it with the broader category leads to bad audio decisions. Here is exactly what separates them, which one matters for your platform, and how to get the best 3D sound out of your gaming headset. Quick Answer Spatial audio is the umbrella term for any technology that simulates 3D sound through headphones. Dolby Atmos is one specific spatial audio format made by Dolby Laboratories, and arguably the most widely supported option for Xbox and PC gaming. PlayStation 5 gamers use Sony's Tempest 3D AudioTech. No matter which format you choose, any quality stereo gaming headset works. The processing happens in software, not hardware. What Is Spatial Audio? Spatial audio refers to any technology that makes sound feel positioned around you in three-dimensional space, above, below, behind, not just left and right. Standard stereo gives you two channels. Spatial audio uses processing algorithms to simulate directional sound through those same two drivers. Multiple technologies fall under this umbrella. Dolby Atmos is available on Xbox, PC, and some mobile devices. Windows Sonic comes free on Xbox and Windows PC. DTS Headphone:X is a paid alternative on select platforms. Sony Tempest 3D AudioTech is built into PS5. Apple Spatial Audio covers Apple devices. Each uses different processing methods, but the goal is identical: convincing your brain that sound is coming from specific positions in 3D space using two speakers in your headset. What Is Dolby Atmos? Dolby Atmos is a specific spatial audio format created by Dolby Laboratories. Originally built for movie theaters, Dolby Atmos treats sounds as individual objects positioned in 3D space, including overhead, rather than locking them to fixed channels like traditional surround sound. For headphones, Dolby Atmos applies head-related transfer function (HRTF) processing to simulate those positioned sounds through stereo drivers (Dolby Laboratories). The result is audio that genuinely feels like it surrounds you from every direction. On Xbox and PC, Dolby Atmos for Headphones requires the Dolby Access app, a one-time purchase of $14.99 from the Microsoft Store (Dolby Access, Microsoft Store). Games with native Dolby Atmos support send positional audio data directly to the Atmos renderer, delivering the most accurate spatial effect possible. How Do the Main Options Compare? Here is how the four main spatial audio formats stack up for headphone gaming: Format Price Platforms Best For Dolby Atmos $14.99 one-time (Dolby Access app) Xbox, PC, mobile Widest native game support, movies Windows Sonic Free Xbox, PC Budget-friendly spatial audio DTS Headphone:X Paid Xbox, PC Alternative to Atmos on select titles Sony Tempest 3D AudioTech Free PS5 only PS5 headphone gaming All four work with any stereo gaming headset , no special hardware required. Dolby Atmos tends to deliver a more spacious, precise soundstage in games that support it natively, while Windows Sonic holds its own as a solid free alternative. DTS performs similarly to Atmos, but fewer games support it natively. On PS5, Dolby Atmos is available through HDMI speaker systems since a September 2023 PlayStation firmware update (PlayStation Blog, September 2023), but for headphone users, Tempest 3D AudioTech remains the go-to and costs nothing extra. Which One Should You Pick for Gaming? Your platform makes this call for you. Xbox Series X|S: Dolby Atmos or Windows Sonic. Atmos offers slightly better spatial accuracy in natively supported games, but Windows Sonic is free and handles positional audio well. Pairing either with a wireless gaming headset that connects directly to your console bypasses controller audio limitations and delivers a cleaner signal. PS5: Sony Tempest 3D AudioTech for headphones. Performance is excellent in PS5 titles, and Tempest works with any stereo headset at no extra cost. PC: Dolby Atmos, Windows Sonic, and DTS are all available. Atmos has the widest native game support and generally provides the best experience for competitive and immersive titles alike. One critical rule applies across every platform, which is to only run one spatial audio solution at a time. Stacking Dolby Atmos through Windows while a game also processes its own spatial audio creates phase conflicts that actually reduce positional accuracy instead of improving it. Can Spatial Audio Help You Hear Footsteps? Adding height information to the audio mix makes a real difference on multi-level maps. Pinpointing whether an enemy is above or below becomes much easier with spatial audio active. That said, some competitive players prefer flat stereo because the simplicity can make left-right directional cues sharper. Test both and see which gives you a better read on enemy positioning. Features like Superhuman Hearing™ on Turtle Beach headsets can further sharpen those critical audio cues for competitive gaming setups . Does Spatial Audio Matter for Music and Movies? Music is where Atmos gets interesting, but only if you are listening to tracks specifically mixed in Dolby Atmos on Apple Music, Tidal, or Amazon Music. Standard stereo tracks do not benefit from Atmos processing, so do not expect a universal upgrade across your entire library. Movies are where Dolby Atmos makes the biggest impact. Films mixed in Atmos on Netflix, Disney+, and Apple TV+ sound noticeably more immersive with overhead and surround effects through headphones. A good wireless headset with cross-platform compatibility pulls double duty here, handling both gaming and movie night without switching gear. Do You Need Special Headphones for Spatial Audio? No. Dolby Atmos, Windows Sonic, Tempest, and every other spatial audio technology work with any stereo headphones or gaming headset. All the processing happens in software. That said, headsets with wider soundstages and clearer drivers make spatial effects significantly more convincing. You do not need "Atmos-certified" or "surround sound" headphones, but investing in a quality pair of wireless gaming headphones with strong audio performance will make every spatial format sound better. The Stealth Pro II pairs Dolby Atmos spatial audio with active noise cancellation and 60mm Eclipse™ Dual Drivers for the full premium experience. The Stealth 700 Gen 3 delivers 60mm Eclipse™ Dual Drivers built for immersive spatial audio, while the Stealth 600 offers rock-solid wireless performance at a lower price point. For budget-conscious gamers, the Recon 70 provides clean wired audio that pairs well with any spatial audio format. Conclusion Spatial audio is the umbrella. Dolby Atmos is the standout option underneath it for Xbox and PC gaming, while Windows Sonic holds its own as a free alternative. PS5 gamers should enable Tempest 3D AudioTech for headphone use. Whichever format fits your platform, pair it with a quality gaming headset that delivers clean audio, and make sure you only run one spatial audio layer at a time. The processing is only as good as the drivers reproducing it. FAQs What is the difference between Dolby Atmos and spatial audio? Spatial audio is the broad category covering any technology that simulates 3D positional sound through headphones. Dolby Atmos is one specific spatial audio format made by Dolby Laboratories. Other options include Windows Sonic, DTS Headphone:X, and Sony Tempest 3D AudioTech. Is Dolby Atmos or spatial audio better for gaming? Dolby Atmos tends to offer slightly better positional accuracy in games that support it natively on Xbox and PC. For PS5, Tempest 3D AudioTech is the primary headphone spatial audio option and performs excellently in supported titles. Is Dolby Atmos the same as spatial audio? No. Dolby Atmos is one type of spatial audio, similar to how a Mustang is one type of car. The two are not competing technologies. Dolby Atmos is a specific format that sits inside the broader spatial audio category alongside Windows Sonic, DTS Headphone:X, and Sony Tempest 3D AudioTech. Does Dolby Atmos help you hear footsteps in games? Spatial audio formats like Dolby Atmos can improve directional awareness, including height detection on multi-level maps. Some competitive players prefer flat stereo for its simplicity, so test both options and see which gives you a better edge. Which is better, Dolby Atmos or DTS spatial audio? Dolby Atmos has broader native game support and wider platform availability across Xbox and PC. DTS Headphone:X performs similarly in terms of audio quality, but fewer games implement it natively. Do you need special headphones for Dolby Atmos? No. Any stereo headphones or gaming headset works with Dolby Atmos and every other spatial audio format. The spatial processing happens entirely in software, though higher-quality headsets with better drivers will make the spatial effects more convincing and accurate.
